verdict.line: You lose if Renekton lands his fury-empowered E-W stun before level 6; you win by surviving to itemize Hydra into Trinity Force, where the 53.1% head-to-head win rate over 452 games takes over.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Reign of Anger fury bar caps at 50 and empowers his next Q or W — an empowered W is a stun, so every fury-full window is a potential kill threat, which is why OP.GG marks both lane and solo-kill advantage to him. Fiora's answer is structural, not a trade you win directly: W (Riposte) parries that exact empowered W, and once both sides hit their item spikes the matchup normalizes hard enough to flip to 53.1% in Fiora's favor over a 452-game sample, despite the defensive laning shape early.

theirWindow.what: He will dash in with E (Slice and Dice), auto, and go for the empowered W stun to lock you for a full Q-auto-auto trade or an Ignite kill. Do not contest CS in melee range when his bar is glowing — back off a step and let him hit minions instead.

yourWindow.when: He E-dashes past minions to hit you
yourWindow.what: That overextension is exactly the OP.GG tip: land Q (Lunge) or an empowered E (Bladework) auto onto a Vitals mark the moment he's in range without his fury loaded. If he goes for the empowered W into you, hold W (Riposte) a beat rather than throwing it preemptively — timed correctly it eats the stun and heals/damages him back.

powerCurve.note: fury sustain wins early Q trades
Riposte and R offset his burst

start.why: The 87.7% pick rate and 53.7% win rate over 464 games reflect the matchup's shape — you need the extra sustain and AD to survive fury-loaded trades, not the shield from Doran's Shield.

boots.why: 82.4% pick, 55.1% win rate over 385 games. Renekton's damage is entirely physical (autos, Q, W, E), so the flat auto-attack reduction directly blunts his all-in windows.

core.why: Highest-win-rate opener (59.8% over 112 games on this exact path) — the healing and cleave let you win extended trades instead of short burst exchanges Renekton favors.
The damage and movement spike is where the lane flips; this is your level 11-13 power curve turn.
Damage-over-time mitigation directly counters Renekton's burst all-in pattern and closes out the late-game sustain war.

situational.when: you're ahead by level 6 and want to snowball burst instead of grinding sustain
the enemy team has anti-heal or your lane sustain war is going long
fights are extending past your first ability rotation and you need ability haste
the enemy team stacks CC beyond Renekton's stun and Plated Steelcaps' armor isn't the priority

runes.keystoneWhy: 61.2% win rate at 9.6% pick — the burst-on-third-hit pattern matches Fiora's empowered E (Bladework) autos landing on Vitals, converting your poke windows into real damage instead of trading fury-for-fury with Conqueror.

summoners.why: 87.1% pick rate and 53.8% win rate. Ignite matters specifically here because Renekton's own kill windows rely on his Cull the Meek sustain — Ignite's healing reduction closes that door if the all-in goes even, and threatens a return kill once his fury dumps.

playing.title: Track the fury bar, not the clock
playing.detail: Don't think in terms of 'early game caution' — think in terms of his fury bar. Every time it nears 50 pre-level 6, assume an E-W stun is coming and disengage from minion range.

playing.title: Hold Riposte for the empowered W
playing.detail: Don't burn W (Riposte) on his normal poke Q. Save it specifically for the empowered W stun — that's the ability it's built to answer, per the OP.GG read on this matchup.

playing.title: Punish overextended E dashes with Vitals hits
playing.detail: When he E-dashes past his own minion wave to reach you, that's your Q (Lunge) or empowered auto window onto a Vitals mark — take it, don't wait for a cleaner setup.

playing.title: Play passive resource control before level 6
playing.detail: You're behind in this window (Renekton has lane and solo-kill advantage). Use Doran's Blade sustain and potions to hold CS parity rather than trying to win trades outright.

playing.title: Flip aggression once Hydra completes
playing.detail: The matchup's win rate lives in the mid-game. Once Ravenous Hydra is up, start initiating trades yourself — the sustain now favors you.

playing.title: Time your ultimate for the kill, not the poke
playing.detail: R (Grand Challenge) executes low-Vitals targets and heals your team on takedown — hold it until he's already below 50% or committed, not as a first-strike tool.

playing.title: Respect Exhaust as an emergency swap
playing.detail: If you're repeatedly losing all-ins despite good play, Exhaust+Flash carries a 55.6% win rate in this matchup (small sample, 3.6% pick) as a direct counter to his burst — situational, not default.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — fury bar timing, Vitals punishes, and the power curve breakdown — is my own tactical read, not sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: Try to block Renekton’s (W) with your [W] by timing it correctly. Hit [P] with your abilities whenever he overextends.
